headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: nullclaw’s broad filesystem/network/tooling can expose Authelia-authenticated data and create unsafe shared-state interactions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Nullclaw can read/write workspace files, use MCP, and run browsers; if it ingests Authelia-protected content or web output, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth but no isolation or provenance controls are documented, so the interaction pathway is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF nullclaw reads Authelia-protected pages, headers, or files into its agent loop
IF MCP or browser output is forwarded into nullclaw prompts without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of web/file content into prompts
Route Authelia outputs through a sanitizer that strips instructions
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Add provenance labels to all forwarded content
requires-engineering: enforce content-type allowlists at the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles authentication flows, while nullclaw reads files, stores secrets, and can write workspace data. If they share a workspace or credentials, nullclaw can expose sensitive auth material to external services through its broad egress, creating a realistic leakage path in default configurations.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or credential store
IF nullclaw forwards workspace contents or secrets to external APIs
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate filesystem namespace
Remove shared credentials from the shared workspace
Restrict nullclaw egress to approved endpoints
Rotate any secrets already present in ~/.nullclaw/workspace
requires-engineering: add per-agent secret scoping and DLP controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Authelia has broad network egress and acts as an auth gateway. If both touch the same repo, config, or deployment artifacts, concurrent writes can corrupt state or produce conflicting auth behavior. No locking or coordination primitive is documented for the pair.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or config directory
IF nullclaw and Authelia are allowed to write without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Freeze git writes while Authelia is active
Use a lock file around shared config edits
Review and merge changes manually before deployment
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: Nullclaw can act on files, webhooks, and shell commands, so if it consumes Authelia-derived outputs as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into downstream actions. Authelia itself is an auth service, not a verifier of nullclaw’s reasoning, so the pair lacks an explicit verification step in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF nullclaw uses Authelia output as a source of truth for actions
IF shell or webhook actions are triggered without human review
mitigations: Require human approval before any action-taking step
Add a verification pass before shell or webhook execution
Log source provenance for every Authelia-derived datum
Limit nullclaw to read-only mode for Authelia outputs
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for inter-agent handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication component with no data-class list, while nullclaw explicitly touches secrets, conversation history, workspace files, and audit logs. If authentication artifacts or user data flow into nullclaw’s workspace or logs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF authentication artifacts or user identifiers are stored in nullclaw workspace files or audit logs
IF retention or deletion requests must be honored across both agents
mitigations: Classify and segregate auth-related data from general workspace files
Set short retention on nullclaw audit logs
Document deletion/export handling for shared records
Review residency of any hosted APIs used by nullclaw
requires-engineering: align retention and subject-rights workflows
